name: Rachel's
label: Quarterstick (Touch and Go)
lede: An art-school guitarist from Rodan and a conservatory violist met on a Baltimore trolley, a Louisville pianist named Rachel taught one of them to read music, and Touch and Go's arthouse label put strings, piano and an orchestral bass drum into indie record stores.

eras.title: Paid in wood, glass and shellac
eras.text: Rachel's took three years to become a band, most of it by phone, mail and tape. Jason Noble was in Louisville starting Rodan, Christian Frederickson was bouncing between conservatories, and Rachel Grimes came in first as a tutor and then as the pianist whose name happened to match the project's.

years.src: The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted' · Touch and Go: Handwriting 30th Anniversary
years.h: An art student and a viola student meet on a Baltimore trolley
years.p: [[Jason Noble|1a30edd1-b7ee-4d9f-ae1c-af8cd4759718]], at art school in Baltimore, and [[Christian Frederickson|fbc379cc-99df-49fe-ad49-94e68b4015d1]], studying at the Peabody Conservatory, start going to each other's openings and recitals. Within months they have a small ensemble playing Noble's compositions.
years.xp:
"They were very clearly art students, and we were very clearly classical music students," Frederickson told the Guardian. He'd go to the art institute for poetry readings; Noble came down to the conservatory for concerts.

The label's history has them meeting "on a crowded trolley." The Guardian's telling has it as a bus.

years.src: Touch and Go: Handwriting 30th Anniversary · Wikipedia: Rachel's
years.h: The first Rachel's tune is paid for with a piece of art
years.p: Tony French, who ran a warehouse studio in Baltimore called the Hat Factory, took a piece of wood, glass and shellac artwork as payment for the session.
years.xp: The name came from an earlier tape some of them had made, Rachel's Halo. The Rachel was Sean Young's replicant in Blade Runner, according to a 2000 Kansas City Star piece cited on Wikipedia.

years.src: Touch and Go: Handwriting 30th Anniversary
years.h: Noble quits art school, goes home to Louisville and starts Rodan
years.p: Artist by day, dishwasher by night, Noble begins playing with friends in the band that becomes [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]]. Frederickson finishes at Peabody, studies in Switzerland, then lands at Juilliard.
years.xp: The label's own history calls what followed "a barrage of telephone, demo tape, notepaper, sheet music & mail communication," with two-week or two-day sessions in whatever city was central enough. Hundreds of 8-track cassettes piled up.

years.src: The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted' · Touch and Go: Handwriting 30th Anniversary
years.h: Rachel Grimes goes from music tutor to the band's pianist
years.p: [[Rachel Grimes|5cd341c1-2b4b-4296-a5c8-147fcb7b2e4e]], a University of Louisville composition student whose band Hula Hoop played shows with Rodan, first helps Noble read written music. By summer 1994 the trio is formally Rachel's.
years.xp:
"I met Jason at a party," Grimes told the Guardian. "He came to my composition recital." The two started writing what she calls introverted piano music together.

The label notes she also brought "the strange coincidence of possessing the name 'Rachel.'"

q: I told him he had to send me a tape.
years.src: The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted'
years.h: Corey Rusk hears the tape and signs them to Quarterstick
years.p: [[Touch and Go|83a554c5-4fd3-4ec8-9dd5-15989850ea17]] owner [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]], who'd put out Rodan's Rusty, had started Quarterstick for music that didn't fit Touch and Go. Talk with Noble about Arvo Pärt, Górecki and Gavin Bryars ended with a request.
years.xp: "He did, I loved it, and the rest is history," Rusk told the Guardian.

eras.title: A debut, a theater score and Neruda
eras.text: A recording project turned into a touring ensemble almost overnight. Grimes, Noble and Frederickson put out a debut built from four years of sessions, then a theater score and a Neruda-inspired album the next year, with a rotating cast from Rodan, The Coctails, Shellac and two symphony orchestras.

years.src: Trouser Press: Rachel's · The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted'
yt: First show, Bop Shop, Chicago, July 1995 (audio)
years.h: Handwriting puts a symphony's worth of guests on Quarterstick
years.p: Seven pieces recorded at various times and places from 1991, with players from [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]], [[The Coctails|0b94e13b-4ee7-448c-be31-5d125d8717ef]] and [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]]'s [[Bob Weston|e87c3bc6-2120-4032-8137-054d0d754b8c]] beside members of two symphony orchestras. It closes with the fourteen-minute 'Full on Night'.
years.xp:
Trouser Press heard 'Full on Night' as something that "wouldn't sound too out of place on a Slint record or the Eraserhead soundtrack." Grimes's solo piece is 'Frida Kahlo'.

The CD came in a letterpress paper sleeve with its own booklet, and demand outran the pressings, the Guardian reports.

years.big: "Tried to pull it off with a serious face"
years.src: The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted'
years.h: Classical purists don't care for bass and drums with their strings
years.p: Indie fans took to Handwriting. Some on the classical side, Rachel Grimes recalls, were deeply insulted by a rock rhythm section next to piano and strings.
years.xp:
"There were a lot of people who seemed deeply insulted that we'd put bass and drums with piano and strings and tried to pull it off with a serious face," Grimes told the Guardian in 2025, smiling.

Frederickson credits timing: labels were hunting independent scenes for the next Nirvana, and an ensemble with a viola got carried along.

years.src: Wikipedia: Music for Egon Schiele · Trouser Press: Rachel's
years.h: Grimes scores the painter Egon Schiele's life for the stage
years.p: Written for the Itinerant Theater Guild's 1995 dance-theater piece about Schiele and recorded in five days that July: just Grimes's piano, Frederickson's viola and cellist Wendy Doyle.
years.xp: Every piece is by Grimes, with titles that walk through the life: 'Egon & Gertie', three self-portrait series, 'Egon & Wally Embrace and Say Farewell'. Rolling Stone's David Fricke called it "the sound of a noble, lonely agony rendered in elegant monochrome."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Sea and the Bells
years.h: Pablo Neruda, a musical saw and Jason Noble on fireworks
years.p: Named for Neruda's poetry collection and recorded from Louisville's university recital hall to Chicago to Juilliard. Cellist [[Eve Miller|0a08cb3c-949f-4729-98ed-869b625a55e6]], drummer [[Edward Grimes|e1270e9a-12d1-4b0b-947c-99505dcde070]] and [[Greg King|28280905-99d0-47c1-b173-001e607f03ed]], credited as boatswain, join the band.
years.xp:
The liner notes credit Noble with recorders, tape sounds and fireworks, Grimes and Noble with a linen sheet, and Jim Maciukenas with musical saw. Edward Grimes, Rachel's brother, plays drum kit on 'Lloyd's Register' and 'His Eyes'.

Paste ranked it the 14th best post-rock album in 2016; Fact had it 16th.

years.src: YouTube: Rachel's live at the Black Cat
yt: Rachel's live at the Black Cat, Nov 19, 1997
years.h: A full Rachel's set at the Black Cat in Washington, on tape
years.p: The ensemble plays the Black Cat in D.C. on its run behind The Sea and the Bells, and the whole show survives on video.

eras.title: The moon, Matmos and a stage too big to tour
eras.text: The records got slower to make and bigger in scope. Selenography took eighteen months across four studios; Systems/Layers started as a theater piece with nine actors and a pit orchestra, and it turned out to be the last album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Selenography
years.h: Selenography is named for mapping the moon's surface
years.p: Recorded from July 1997 to January 1999 in Chicago, Louisville, Philadelphia and at Pachyderm in Cannon Falls, Minnesota. [[Uzeda|9cb56cf1-bd4a-4d59-8ecb-dc412f595dd3]]'s Giovanna Cacciola sings on two tracks.
years.xp:
Frederickson's credits run to coins, gutter rattle, bowed gutter and "fake instruments". His piece 'The Mysterious Disappearance of Louis LePrince' is named for the film pioneer who vanished in 1890. The aerial photographs are by Adriel Heisey.

Pitchfork gave it 8.0; NME 5/10.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rachel's · The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted'
years.h: A split disc with Matmos, named for Handwriting's long closer
years.p: Full On Night, shared with San Francisco electronic duo [[Matmos|46e8a8ee-d2cd-4165-9725-02f72d0027a9]], comes out on Quarterstick.

years.src: Wikipedia: Systems/Layers
years.h: Systems/Layers, made with New York's SITI Company
years.p: Nineteen short pieces from a dance-theater collaboration, with Shannon Wright singing and SITI actors' voices threaded through. It reached No. 16 on Billboard's Classical Albums chart.
years.xp: Filmmaker Jem Cohen is among the voices; Greg King is credited with films. Metacritic's average was 81. The Times called it the band's worst album; PopMatters called it one of the year's finest.

q: We created a piece of art that was just completely unaffordable.
years.src: The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted' · Wikipedia: Systems/Layers
years.h: Nine actors, projections and a live pit orchestra
years.p: The staged Systems/Layers with the Saratoga International Theater Institute left the musicians exhausted, Rachel Grimes says, and broke the budget.
years.xp:
"We never, ever thought practically about the cheapest way to tour," Grimes told the Guardian. The SITI Company and its students at Utah State University and Skidmore College performed it live.

It was the last Rachel's album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rachel's
years.h: Technology Is Killing Music EP on Three Lobed
years.p: The last Rachel's release, an EP for Three Lobed Recordings.

eras.title: Hollywood calls, two members die
eras.text: After 2005 the band's music kept turning up in films while its members moved on. Jason Noble died in 2012 and Edward Grimes in 2017.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rachel's · The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted'
years.h: 'Water from the Same Source' lands in Hancock
years.p: The Will Smith film uses it, though it isn't on the soundtrack album. Paolo Sorrentino later puts it in The Great Beauty.
years.xp: Other placements Wikipedia lists: 'Lloyd's Register' in Une liaison pornographique, 'Even/Odd' in Reha Erdem's Kosmos, 'NY Snow Globe' in 2017's War Machine. Paul Murray's novel An Evening of Long Goodbyes takes its title from a Selenography track.

years.src: Louisville Public Media: Musician Jason Noble Dies
years.h: Jason Noble dies at 40 during a cancer trial
years.p: Noble died at the National Institutes of Health in Bethesda, Maryland, where he was in a clinical trial. He had been diagnosed with synovial sarcoma in 2009.
years.xp: Louisville Public Media remembered him for [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]], Rachel's and [[Shipping News|d6ed84da-0414-4c44-ace7-ae491ce7d999]], a band that grew out of his composition work for This American Life. He'd also worked for years at the record store ear X-Tacy and wrote a music and art column for LEO.

years.src: The Interior Journal: Edward Sterling Grimes · Wikipedia: Rachel's
years.h: Edward Grimes, the band's drummer, dies at 43
years.p: Rachel Grimes's brother, the band's longtime drummer, died of natural causes, his family's obituary said.

eras.title: Back in print, on silver
eras.text: Grimes kept composing and Frederickson went to teach at MIT. Thirty years on, Touch and Go reissued the debut, and the two surviving founders talked about it.

years.src: The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted'
years.h: Grimes premieres The Way Forth, a Kentucky folk opera
years.p: Rachel Grimes's opera follows women's voices through Kentucky history. The research led her to the enslaved violinist and bandleader Henry Hart, whose music she is preparing to publish.

years.src: Touch and Go: Handwriting 30th Anniversary · The Guardian: 'People seemed deeply insulted'
years.h: Thirty years on, Handwriting returns on 500 silver LPs
years.p: Touch and Go reissues the debut with a jacket screen-printed by Dexterity Press and a 16-page booklet, plus sheet music for three of its pieces.
years.xp: "It's weird and hard but that's what it is to miss the people you love," Grimes told the Guardian. "Being in a band with my brother and my friends was such a fun romp."
